item.title: Tuvalu National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Tuvalu National Day

Press Statement

September 30, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend my congratulations to the people of Tuvalu on your 48th National Day.

The bilateral relationship between the United States and Tuvalu rests on a foundation of mutual respect and a shared vision for a stable and prosperous Pacific region.  The United States is committed to strengthening our cooperation on trade, investment, and regional security in the years ahead.

I wish you and all Tuvaluans a spirited celebration of your independence.

item.title: Palau National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Palau National Day

Press Statement

September 30, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend warm congratulations to the people of Palau as you celebrate your national day.

Palau remains one of the United States’ most trusted partners in the Pacific.  Our partnership, rooted in mutual respect and trust, has grown significantly stronger the past year. We continue to work together to advance regional security and economic growth that benefit all Pacific nations.

 On this special day, the United States reaffirms its commitment, underpinned by the Compact of Free Association, to strengthening our partnership with Palau and supporting its continued leadership in advancing peace and prosperity across the Pacific.

I extend my best wishes to all Palauans as you commemorate this important day and your nation’s achievements.

item.title: G20 Chair’s Statement: Ebola Ministerial on Accelerating Collective Action to Defeat Ebola
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

G20 Chair’s Statement: Ebola Ministerial on Accelerating Collective Action to Defeat Ebola

Media Note

September 30, 2026

The United States convened a G20 Foreign Ministerial to reaffirm its commitment to accelerating collective action against the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The G20 and other major donors announced more than $470 million in new commitments, surpassing $2 billion in total global pledges since the outbreak began in May 2026. As the current holder of the G20 Presidency, the United States invited other major health and humanitarian donors to the Foreign Ministerial on Ebola—including Poland, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Singapore, Qatar, and the UAE—along with key organizations such as the Africa CDC, OCHA, the Pandemic Fund, UNICEF, and the World Bank.

We commend the health care workers, volunteers, and local communities battling this disease, which—as President Trump and other G7 Leaders recognized in June—poses unique challenges: it is centered in an isolated, conflict-affected area, and existing vaccines, diagnostics, and therapies are not fully effective against this Bundibugyo strain. Global actors must scale up response activities across outbreak zones and strengthen preparedness in high-risk areas, including contact tracing, protecting frontline responders, expanding bed capacity, deploying new diagnostics, and investing in vaccine development. This disease can be defeated, as shown by the successful end of Uganda’s outbreak in August.

To advance these goals, the United States announced an additional $267 million in health and humanitarian assistance, bringing the U.S. Government’s direct assistance to $887 million. This new funding will support Ebola treatment units, broader health services, safe and dignified burial teams, mass procurements of personal protective equipment, expanded surveillance, and contact tracing through trusted local implementers. In addition to this direct Ebola funding, this year we have mobilized $350 million in broader humanitarian assistance to the region through our global partnership with OCHA.

The following G20 members and other donors announced new funding commitments for the Ebola response during the G20 Foreign Ministerial on Accelerating Collective Action to Defeat Ebola:

  • Australia announced $3.5 million (5 million AUD) to the Ebola response.
  • France announced $16 million to the Ebola response bringing its total to $34 million.
  • Germany announced an additional $24.8 million (€21.8 million), bringing its total funding to $30.7 million to support laboratories, expand treatment capacity, train health workers, and strengthen health care and risk communication in communities.
  • Italy announced $11.3 million (€10 million), bringing its total to $14.5 million (€12.8 million) to support clinical trials to assess the efficacy of the deployment of new vaccines, provisioning essential medical supplies, and to support prevention efforts.
  • Japan announced an additional $5 million in emergency grant aid, bringing its total support near $12.4 million to use in the most severely affected region. The assistance aims to build technical capacity and dispatch experts.
  • The Republic of Korea announced a new commitment of $18 million to support the Ebola response, through global health partners, contributing to international efforts to strengthen access to vaccines, therapeutics, and other medical countermeasures.
  • The United Kingdom announced a new $67.5 million (£50 million) funding package, bringing its total support to $105.6 million (£78.7) million, to strengthen disease surveillance, support frontline health workers, and expand access to treatment.
  • United Arab Emirates announced $10 million to the Ebola response.
  • The World Bank announced $90 million to the Ebola response–$80 million from the Crisis Response Window and $10 million from the Global Financing Facility to protect essential health services.

item.title: U.S. Tightens Cuba Sanctions to Counter Regime Repression
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

U.S. Tightens Cuba Sanctions to Counter Regime Repression

Press Statement

September 30, 2026

This week, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) published new Cuba Sanctions Regulations implementing President Trump’s Executive Order 14404, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and Threats to the United States National Security and Foreign Policy,” which invokes the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) to significantly broaden and sharpen sanctions and economic pressure on Communist Cuba, its repressive military and intelligence apparatus, subversive and terror networks, and financial enablers. Treasury also amended the longstanding Cuban Assets Control Regulations (CACR) to close loopholes the Cuban regime has long exploited to engage in sanctions evasion, enrich regime insiders, and fund dangerous subversive and military activities which threaten the national security of the United States.

The Trump Administration remains committed to leveraging all available sanctions authorities to drive meaningful reform in Cuba, support the Cuban people’s aspirations for freedom, and hold accountable the individuals and entities that pose a threat to the national security of the United States.

For more information on the new and amended regulations, see the Department of the Treasury’s website.

item.title: Sanctioning Money Launderers Linked to Tren de Aragua’s Multi-Million-Dollar Theft Scheme
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Sanctioning Money Launderers Linked to Tren de Aragua’s Multi-Million-Dollar Theft Scheme

Press Statement

September 30, 2026

The Trump Administration will not allow Foreign Terrorist Organizations to victimize our citizens or financial institutions.  The United States is sanctioning 11 targets linked to Tren de Aragua (TdA), including 10 involved in a scheme that stole millions of dollars from U.S. financial institutions as well as one alleged TdA leader involved in illicit gold mining operations.  These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

One of the FBI’s 10 Most Wanted Fugitives, Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, a.k.a. “Prometheus,” orchestrated the scheme, through which cash is stolen from U.S.-based automated teller machines (ATMs) using malicious software that criminals install on the ATMs, forcing them to dispense cash.  The stolen cash is then laundered and funneled to TdA members. 

Separately, TdA leader Juan Gabriel Rivas Nunez, a.k.a. “Juancho,” operated out of multiple South American countries and was allegedly involved in illicit gold mining operations, narcotics exporting, and violent crime.

This is a warning to anyone who finances or does business with TdA:  Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States is coming for you and your assets, no matter where you hide.  Your days exploiting the American people are coming to an end.

Today’s action was taken pursuant to E.O. 13581, which targets transnational criminal organizations, as amended by E.O. 13863, and E.O. 13224, as amended, which targets terrorists and their supporters. 

For more information about today’s sanctions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Botswana National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Botswana National Day

Press Statement

September 30, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Botswana as you celebrate 60 years of independence.

This milestone anniversary is a testament to Botswana’s democratic traditions and the resilience of the Batswana people. The United States is proud to stand alongside Botswana as a trusted partner, from our continued collaboration on public health through initiatives that have improved the lives of countless Batswana to new efforts to expand trade and investment that create jobs and opportunity for both nations. We look forward to deepening this partnership in the years ahead as we work together to unlock Botswana’s economic potential.

item.title: Sanctioning Sinaloa Cartel Leaders and Corrupt Enablers in Baja California
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Sanctioning Sinaloa Cartel Leaders and Corrupt Enablers in Baja California

Press Statement

September 29, 2026

The United States is today sanctioning 21 individuals and 25 entities tied to the Sinaloa Cartel, including cartel leader Ismael Zambada Sicairos (“Mayito Flaco”) and the network of Tijuana- and Mexicali-based cell leaders, financial facilitators, and corrupt Mexican officials who enable the cartel to operate with impunity along the U.S.-Mexico border.

This action underscores the Trump Administration’s commitment to dismantling the Sinaloa Cartel’s operational and political infrastructure in Mexico, disrupting the networks that fuel fentanyl trafficking, violence, and corruption, and threaten communities on both sides of the border. Today’s designations reflect the whole-of-government approach the United States is taking to combat transnational criminal organizations and the Foreign Terrorist Organizations with which they intersect.

Today’s designations highlight the corrosive reach of cartel influence into Mexican governance, particularly in Baja California, where associates of the governor’s ex-husband, a former Mexicali public security director, and other political operators allegedly accepted bribes to shield Sinaloa Cartel operations from law enforcement.

To accelerate the removal of key cartel figures from the region, the Department of State’s Narcotics Rewards Program is offering up to $5 million each for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Tijuana plaza bosses Alfonso Arzate Garcia (“Aquiles”) and Rene Arzate Garcia (“La Rana”), as well as up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Mexicali cartel leader Juan Jose Ponce Felix (“El Ruso”).

The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886, which targets terrorists and their supporters. For more information about today’s designations, please see Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio at President Trump’s America.gov Event
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Washington, D.C.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio at President Trump’s America.gov Event

Remarks

September 29, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.  That was actually pretty amazing there by Dr. Oz.  That actually was remarkable.  This is – this is really going to be a revolution in the way that government works for the average American.  So just think about for a moment what you just saw.  They took something that millions of Americans deal with every single day, and they made it simpler and they made it easier and they made it more effective, and they made it that way in every possible way.  And that’s just one piece of the whole that we’re here to talk about today. 

So earlier this year, Joe came to my office and he showed me America.gov.  It’s a whole-of-government project.  And it touches on every department, every agency, every bureau you can imagine.  And in each and every case, the goal is simple.  It’s to make life better and easier for normal Americans.  So, you’ve already heard a few examples already. 

Now, for us at the State Department, one particular thing came to mind: the passport.  Today, more than half of Americans have one, and it has come a long way since the early days of this country.  Let me show you – this is what it looked like in 1781, just a piece of paper.  It’s a very nice one, but just a piece of paper.  And then in time, that piece of paper became a booklet.  That booklet then introduced a photograph.  And then we entered the computer age with electronic chips.  From the wax seal to the electronic chip, the American passport has become the most trusted and powerful – and I would argue most important – identity document in the entire world. 

But the document kept evolving.  Unfortunately, the process of getting one did not continue to evolve.  So today, if you need your first passport, you start at the State Department’s website, and this is what greets you.  This is what greets you.  It’s not bad.  There’s a lot of information up there, but it’s – but if you actually want to apply, that is where the maze starts.  So you have to know which form to print, you have to schedule an appointment, then you have to go wait in line, and then when something – and when something is this hard, then someone is bound to make money off of it, right? 

So today, there’s an entire cottage industry that’s built around cashing in on every stage of the passport process.  And some of these sites are charging you for forms that are free; some are charging you for appointments that are free.  And after they take your money, they take your most sensitive personal information too.  And if you make it through all of that, sometime in the future, you get this in the mail.  This is what arrives, and that’s not really the kind of packaging you would expect for the most powerful identity document you will ever receive.  We ship tens of millions of these envelopes every year. 

Now, a United States passport, it means something, right?  It’s a physical symbol of who we are.  It’s a promise that, wherever you go in the world as an American, you are one of us.  And so, I think – I think you would agree – that American citizens deserve better than this.  And that’s why the State Department is partnering with America.gov to rebuild the entire thing from the ground up, and it begins with something pretty remarkable. 

Starting next year, Americans will be able to apply for their first passport entirely online.  (Applause.) 

Let me show you how easy it is.  You would ask:  How do I apply for my first passport?  And once I’m signed-in with login.gov, I can securely see the information that the government already has about me in its system.  I don’t have to type the same thing over and over and over again. 

Now the fun part, the photo.  You can take a new one of them yourself on the phone.  You probably can’t use those filters to make you look 50 years younger, but you can take a picture of yourself on the phone in the comfort of your own home, or you can upload one directly from your own device.  You’re not going any longer to some drugstore to get your picture taken behind a white screen.  And this is a really cool feature:  You can see your photo in the context of the finished passport.  And if you don’t like it – and as you probably know, many people don’t like it, so you’re going to take 150 of these.  (Laughter.)  But eventually, you will like one.  And you can retake it until it’s the perfect shot, the one you like. 

Now, I have to say, this may be the most beautiful government checkout I’ve ever seen.  And because I’m securely logged in through login.gov, my name, my address – they’re already here.  I enter my payment securely.  So, let’s check out.  And that’s it.  There, your payment is complete, my first application.  (Applause.) 

No printing forms, no drugstore hostage photo – (laughter) – no appointment, no line, no middleman that you’re paying to do something that should be available to you.  You tell America.gov what you’re trying to do, and it walks you through every single step and tells you exactly what comes next.

And then there’s this – real-time status.  So, for years, you could track any delivery – a pizza, whatever – more precisely than you can track where your passport is in the mail.  Not anymore.  We have an estimated delivery date, so you know it’s coming. 

And by the end of 2027, our goal is for the vast majority of Americans to be able to apply for a passport or a passport card on America.gov.  Because the point of all of this, we’re doing here today – and this is simple – make the process more accessible and easier for Americans.  So, whether you live in the middle of a major city or you live in a rural town, you’ll be able to apply from anywhere.

Now, there’s one more thing. 

(Video is played.)  (Applause.)

SECRETARY RUBIO:  That looks pretty good.  I actually carry these around with me now.  There it is.  It looks even better in person.  (Applause.)  This is the 2028 U.S. passport.  And the State Department worked really closely with the National Design Studio to rethink it from cover to cover.  Because a passport – think about this – a passport is more than just a travel document.  It’s an expression of the unbreakable bond between the nation and the citizen –  a bond, by the way, that doesn’t end at the water’s edge, at our borders, but one that Americans carry with them.  You carry this with you when you travel to any corner and every corner of the globe.

And so, we found one uniquely American symbol to carry that idea from beginning to end.  You see it carved into our buildings.  You see it on the ships that defended and defend our country.  You see it on our currency.  And when our founders needed a symbol of the country itself, they placed it at the center of the Great Seal.  So frankly, there was really only one choice – the American Eagle, the emblem of American strength and freedom – and it’s instantly recognizable to everyone anywhere in the world.

Now, the eagle has always been on the cover of the passport, but Joe and his team at the design studio helped us make it even better.  So now that’s the old passport, right?  That’s the new one.  The words “United States of America” are now exactly where they belong – first, right on top – and the Great Seal is larger, it’s more prominent, it’s more gold.  (Laughter.)

And when you open the book – when you open the book, the eagle takes flight.  The eagle carries you across 250 years of America.  You see it soar, right, from the eagle’s point of view, above patriots standing their ground at Lexington and past the families crossing west with everything they owned in a wagon.  The men who drove steel across a continent and two bicycle mechanics from Ohio who taught mankind how to fly.  There’s the Marines who raised our flag on Iwo Jima and all the way to the Artemis splashdown.  The entire sweep of American history from the patriots of ’76, to the pioneers setting out into the great unknown, to the astronauts who carried our flag to the moon.

It is a visual story of the greatest nation in the history of the world – a nation destined from the very beginning for extraordinary things.  And this passport won’t just carry you; it will carry that story into the world.  And because this is the – because this is one of the most secure documents in the world, there are obviously things that I can’t and won’t show you, but here’s what I can show you.  I can show you this.  Watch the eagle as you flip through the pages.  It flies.  Now, I think that’s pretty good.  (Applause.)

I can see Americans sitting at airports all over the world, like why do people keep flipping through the page?  (Laughter.)  Well, it’s a – it’s either this or some Gameboy for your kids to keep them entertained, they can flip the eagle around.  But anyway, the book itself is beautiful.  It’s incredibly secure.  It feels substantial.  And after putting this much thought into the book itself, we figured that the way it arrives at your home ought to matter, too.  The presentation, how it gets there, should matter.

So, you remember this.  I showed this to you earlier, right?  We’re not doing that anymore.  For something as important and as dignified as the United States passport, it will arrive the way you would expect it to.  This is what comes next.  (Applause.)

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Washington, D.C.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio at President Trump’s America.gov Event

Remarks

September 29, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.  That was actually pretty amazing there by Dr. Oz.  That actually was remarkable.  This is – this is really going to be a revolution in the way that government works for the average American.  So just think about for a moment what you just saw.  They took something that millions of Americans deal with every single day, and they made it simpler and they made it easier and they made it more effective, and they made it that way in every possible way.  And that’s just one piece of the whole that we’re here to talk about today. 

So earlier this year, Joe came to my office and he showed me America.gov.  It’s a whole-of-government project.  And it touches on every department, every agency, every bureau you can imagine.  And in each and every case, the goal is simple.  It’s to make life better and easier for normal Americans.  So, you’ve already heard a few examples already. 

Now, for us at the State Department, one particular thing came to mind: the passport.  Today, more than half of Americans have one, and it has come a long way since the early days of this country.  Let me show you – this is what it looked like in 1781, just a piece of paper.  It’s a very nice one, but just a piece of paper.  And then in time, that piece of paper became a booklet.  That booklet then introduced a photograph.  And then we entered the computer age with electronic chips.  From the wax seal to the electronic chip, the American passport has become the most trusted and powerful – and I would argue most important – identity document in the entire world. 

But the document kept evolving.  Unfortunately, the process of getting one did not continue to evolve.  So today, if you need your first passport, you start at the State Department’s website, and this is what greets you.  This is what greets you.  It’s not bad.  There’s a lot of information up there, but it’s – but if you actually want to apply, that is where the maze starts.  So you have to know which form to print, you have to schedule an appointment, then you have to go wait in line, and then when something – and when something is this hard, then someone is bound to make money off of it, right? 

So today, there’s an entire cottage industry that’s built around cashing in on every stage of the passport process.  And some of these sites are charging you for forms that are free; some are charging you for appointments that are free.  And after they take your money, they take your most sensitive personal information too.  And if you make it through all of that, sometime in the future, you get this in the mail.  This is what arrives, and that’s not really the kind of packaging you would expect for the most powerful identity document you will ever receive.  We ship tens of millions of these envelopes every year. 

Now, a United States passport, it means something, right?  It’s a physical symbol of who we are.  It’s a promise that, wherever you go in the world as an American, you are one of us.  And so, I think – I think you would agree – that American citizens deserve better than this.  And that’s why the State Department is partnering with America.gov to rebuild the entire thing from the ground up, and it begins with something pretty remarkable. 

Starting next year, Americans will be able to apply for their first passport entirely online.  (Applause.) 

Let me show you how easy it is.  You would ask:  How do I apply for my first passport?  And once I’m signed-in with login.gov, I can securely see the information that the government already has about me in its system.  I don’t have to type the same thing over and over and over again. 

Now the fun part, the photo.  You can take a new one of them yourself on the phone.  You probably can’t use those filters to make you look 50 years younger, but you can take a picture of yourself on the phone in the comfort of your own home, or you can upload one directly from your own device.  You’re not going any longer to some drugstore to get your picture taken behind a white screen.  And this is a really cool feature:  You can see your photo in the context of the finished passport.  And if you don’t like it – and as you probably know, many people don’t like it, so you’re going to take 150 of these.  (Laughter.)  But eventually, you will like one.  And you can retake it until it’s the perfect shot, the one you like. 

Now, I have to say, this may be the most beautiful government checkout I’ve ever seen.  And because I’m securely logged in through login.gov, my name, my address – they’re already here.  I enter my payment securely.  So, let’s check out.  And that’s it.  There, your payment is complete, my first application.  (Applause.) 

No printing forms, no drugstore hostage photo – (laughter) – no appointment, no line, no middleman that you’re paying to do something that should be available to you.  You tell America.gov what you’re trying to do, and it walks you through every single step and tells you exactly what comes next.

And then there’s this – real-time status.  So, for years, you could track any delivery – a pizza, whatever – more precisely than you can track where your passport is in the mail.  Not anymore.  We have an estimated delivery date, so you know it’s coming. 

And by the end of 2027, our goal is for the vast majority of Americans to be able to apply for a passport or a passport card on America.gov.  Because the point of all of this, we’re doing here today – and this is simple – make the process more accessible and easier for Americans.  So, whether you live in the middle of a major city or you live in a rural town, you’ll be able to apply from anywhere.

Now, there’s one more thing. 

(Video is played.)  (Applause.)

And so, we found one uniquely American symbol to carry that idea from beginning to end.  You see it carved into our buildings.  You see it on the ships that defended and defend our country.  You see it on our currency.  And when our founders needed a symbol of the country itself, they placed it at the center of the Great Seal.  So frankly, there was really only one choice – the American Eagle, the emblem of American strength and freedom – and it’s instantly recognizable to everyone anywhere in the world.

So, I hope you’ll get one, and thank you for the opportunity to present this to you today.  (Applause.)  Thank you.  (Applause.)

item.title: United States Disrupts Iran’s Proliferation-Sensitive Efforts in Support of UN Restrictions Fact Sheet
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

United States Disrupts Iran’s Proliferation-Sensitive Efforts in Support of UN Restrictions Fact Sheet

Fact Sheet

September 29, 2026

Today, following the one-year anniversary of the reimposition of the UN sanctions and restrictive measures on Iran, the Department of State is designating one Iran-based entity and two Russia-based entities involved in facilitating Iran’s military procurement efforts and the transport of arms and related materiel to and from Iran, including violations of the renewed UN measures.  Over the past year, the United States has worked relentlessly with partners to enforce these restrictions, imposing dozens of new sanctions, convening representatives from 40 countries to strengthen implementation, and submitting updated identifying information on sanctioned entities to support industry implementation.

Under Operation Economic Outcast, the United States is committed to disrupting the procurement efforts of Iran’s military programs and denying Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) access to assets and resources that sustain its destabilizing activities.  This action underscores the United States’ resolve to prevent Iran from reconstituting its proliferation-sensitive programs.

The U.S. Department of State’s Rewards for Justice program is authorized under 22 U.S.C. §  2708 to offer a reward for information that disrupts the financial mechanisms of the IRGC, a U.S.-designated Foreign Terrorist Organization.

All Department of State sanctions targets are being designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13949, which targets certain persons with respect to the conventional arms activities of Iran.

The Department of the Treasury is concurrently designating ten entities and individuals who have procured weapons and weapons components for Iran’s Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL).  For more information on these actions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

Designations Pursuant to Section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949  

  • JOINT STOCK COMPANY EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN BUREAU NAMED AFTER A.S. YAKOVLEV (YAKOVLEV) is a Russia-based aircraft manufacturer that develops and produces the Yak-130 advanced trainer fighter jet. Russia first delivered several Yak-130 aircraft to Iran in late 2023. In November 2025, Russia delivered additional equipment associated with Yak-130 combat aircraft to Iran. These were transferred to Iran aboard a U.S.-sanctioned Russian aircraft from a manufacturing facility associated with the YAKOVLEV in Irkutsk, Russia.  In December 2025, Russia delivered several shipments of additional equipment associated with Yak-130 combat aircraft equipment to Iran from the same manufacturing facility in Irkutsk, Russia, associated with YAKOVLEV.  Russia has now delivered to Iran nearly all of its reportedly 24 contracted Yak-130 aircraft.  YAKOVLEV was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 14024 on May 19, 2023.  YAKOVLEV is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949 for having engaged, or attempted to engage, in any activity that materially contributes to, or poses a risk of materially contributing to, the proliferation of arms or related materiel or items intended for military end-uses or military end-users, including any efforts to manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, transport, transfer, or use such items, by the Government of Iran (including persons owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of the Government of Iran) or paramilitary organizations financially or militarily supported by the Government of Iran.
  • MG-FLOT LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (MG-FLOT) is a Russia-based shipping company whose vessels transport weapons for the Russian government. In 2024, MG-FLOT vessels were involved in the transfer of close-range ballistic missiles (CRBMs) from Iran to Russia.  In late 2025, Iran delivered air defense vehicles and related materiel from Iran to Russia aboard Russian roll-on roll-off motor vessel Kompozitor Rakhmaninov.  Kompozitor Rakhmaninov is a Russian flagged vessel identified as blocked property of MG-FLOT.  On June 27, 2022, TransMorFlot LLC changed its name to MG-FLOT.  TransMorFlot LLC was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 14024 on May 8, 2022.  MG-FLOT is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949 for having engaged, or attempted to engage, in any activity that materially contributes to, or poses a risk of materially contributing to, the proliferation of arms or related materiel or items intended for military end-uses or military end-users, including any efforts to manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, transport, transfer, or use such items, by the Government of Iran (including persons owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of the Government of Iran) or paramilitary organizations financially or militarily supported by the Government of Iran.
  • SAHA AIRLINES is an Iran-based airline affiliated with the Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force (IRIAF) and has been involved in efforts by Iran to transport arms and related materiel. SAHA AIRLINES was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 on September 8, 2026.  SAHA AIRLINES is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949 for having engaged, or attempted to engage, in any activity that materially contributes to, or poses a risk of materially contributing to, the proliferation of arms or related materiel or items intended for military end-uses or military end-users, including any efforts to manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, transport, transfer, or use such items, by the Government of Iran (including persons owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of the Government of Iran) or paramilitary organizations financially or militarily supported by the Government of Iran.

Sanctions Implications

As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 13949, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).  In addition, all entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. 

All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt.  These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.   

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. 

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov.  Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

Rewards for Justice seeks information on the financial activities of the following key leaders of the IRGC Aerospace Force (IRGC-ASF), which facilitates operations, develops weapons, and procures equipment for the IRGC’s terrorist activities.

  • IRGC BRIGADIER GENERAL ABDOLLAH MEHRABI is chief of the IRGC-ASF Research and Self-Sufficiency Jihad Organization (SSJO), which is responsible for the analysis and development of weapons utilized to attack U.S. armed forces personnel and infrastructure in the Middle East. Mehrabi has overseen significant advances in military satellites and drone manufacturing. As co-owner of the Oje Parvaz Mado Nafar Company, a manufacturer of engines used in Iran’s Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 UAVs, Mehrabi has acquired components for the production of Iranian Shahed drones launched against the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet in Bahrain.  
  • AHMED JA’FARABADI is a senior IRGC-ASF official who is directly involved in the organization’s operations and logistics processes.    
  • ALI ASGHAR NOROUZI is the chairman of the IRGC Cooperative Foundation. The foundation serves as a slush fund for the IRGC’s personnel and their business interests. In his position as a senior IRGC officer, Norouzi has played a crucial role in the transfer of funds and weapons to allied armed proxies in the Middle East.
